result.instructions: Tools for Street.co.uk, hosted by usefulapi.io. If the user is new or asks what this server can do, suggest requests such as: "Which viewings are booked for tomorrow and who are the applicants?"; "List the sales applicants with a hot lead rating whose follow-up is overdue."; "Show the properties that went under offer this month in my main branch.". Read-only tools never change data; ask the user before a tool that creates, changes or deletes Street.co.uk data. Free plan: 50 tool calls per month. Run street_usage_status to see the calls used this month. If the user asks for something none of these tools can do, tell the user and, with their OK, run street_request_feature to record the request. Paid plan: Pro (unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month), $9/month or $90/year). Pro can be cancelled at any time and then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. When the user wants more calls or reaches the limit, run street_upgrade (plan "monthly" or "yearly"); it returns a payment link for the user to open. street_cancel_subscription cancels Pro at the end of the paid period.

tools.name: street_create_enquiry
tools.title: Create enquiry
tools.description: WRITE: record a new inbound enquiry (a lead) in Street. Street matches the email address to an existing person or creates one, and the agency's own automations may then email or assign the lead. Street requires the enquiry to be tied to exactly one record: pass property_id, or sales_applicant_id, or lettings_applicant_id. Pass the same enquiry_identifier on a retry: Street then returns the existing enquiry instead of creating a duplicate. POST /enquiries.

postcode.description: Enquirer's UK postcode (stored only when a new person is created).

property_id.description: Property UUID the enquiry is about (street_list_properties).

sales_applicant_id.description: Sales applicant UUID the enquiry belongs to (street_list_sales_applicants).

lettings_applicant_id.description: Lettings applicant UUID the enquiry belongs to (street_list_lettings_applicants).

branch_id.description: Branch UUID to route the enquiry to (street_list_branches).

custom_source.description: One or two words naming the origin, e.g. website (max 25 characters).

enquiry_identifier.description: Your own stable id for this enquiry, prefixed with your integration name. Makes a retry safe.

request_viewing.description: The enquirer asks for a viewing.

request_valuation.description: The enquirer asks for a valuation.

property_to_sell.description: The enquirer has a property to sell.

property_to_let.description: The enquirer has a property to let.

tools.name: street_create_note
tools.title: Create note
tools.description: WRITE: add a note to one Street record (a person, property, applicant, sale, viewing, tenancy and so on). The note is visible to the agency's staff. Not idempotent: calling it twice adds two notes. POST /notes.

target_type.description: The kind of record the note goes on.

pinned.description: Pin the note to the top.

author_id.description: UUID of the Street user to show as the author (street_list_users). Default: the token's user.

tools.name: street_create_task
tools.title: Create task
tools.description: WRITE: create a task (to-do) in Street, optionally assigned to a user and given a task type. Not idempotent: calling it twice creates two tasks. POST /todos.

user_id.description: UUID of the user to assign the task to (street_list_users).

note.description: An extra note stored with the task.

tools.name: street_create_follow_up
tools.title: Create follow-up
tools.description: WRITE: schedule a follow-up on a property, sales or lettings applicant, sale or valuation. Not idempotent: calling it twice creates two follow-ups. POST /follow-ups.

target_type.description: The kind of record the follow-up belongs to.

tools.name: street_create_maintenance_request
tools.title: Create maintenance request
tools.description: WRITE: log a maintenance request against a property (a request, not a job: Street staff turn it into a job). Not idempotent: calling it twice logs two requests. POST /maintenance-requests.

tools.name: street_update_person
tools.title: Update person
tools.description: WRITE: change a person's title, name, marketing consent or contact preferences in Street. Street requires both names on every update, so the current record is read first and anything you leave out is sent back unchanged. Contact details (email, phone, address) cannot be changed through the API. PATCH /people/{id}.

title.description: Title such as Mr, Mrs, Dr; null clears it.

marketing_consent.description: Whether the person agreed to marketing.
